basis: Hosted SaaS: hosting, SSL, custom domain and upgrades are included in every plan (pricing page); no server or CLI needed to open a store; theme editor and apps for most needs
Web installer and a back office with guided onboarding, but the merchant must provide PHP/MySQL hosting and choose modules (system requirements page); more steps than SaaS
Composer install plus search engine (OpenSearch), cache store, cron and database tuning (system requirements 2.4.9); admin is powerful but large; steepest learning curve for merchants and developers
Plugin installed in an existing WordPress site (wizard in the admin); familiar editor and page-builder ecosystem, but the merchant still owns hosting, themes and plugin choices
Shopify patches and upgrades the platform; remaining work is quarterly API version migration (each stable version supported at least 12 months) and app/theme updates
Self-hosted: merchant applies minor releases (at most two per year, previous minor stops receiving patches) and module updates; 8.2 extended support until 10.0.0; no EOL dates published
Monthly security bulletins (7 APSB bulletins in 2026 to date, one out-of-band zero-day) and a three-year support window per 2.4.x line; patching and upgrades are heavy projects
Release about every five weeks plus WordPress, PHP, theme and plugin updates; security backports only to the last 21 major versions at CVSS >= 9; host-level work stays with the merchant
Built-in checkout, POS, markets, B2B on higher plans, Flow automation, Functions and a large app store (about 32,000 apps detected by Store Leads); advanced checkout control is Plus-only
Catalogue, multistore, 9.2 adds one-page checkout and improved B2B (beta flags); breadth beyond the core comes from paid Addons modules
Most complete core among the four: multi-source inventory, multistore, B2B and layered pricing in the Adobe Commerce edition, GraphQL and REST APIs, Page Builder
Core covers catalogue, orders and blocks checkout; most advanced features come from extensions (10,039 plugins tagged woocommerce on WordPress.org) and WordPress itself

Platform patched centrally by Shopify without customer action; public bug bounty; CVEs exist only for open-source libraries (21 NVD CVEs by vendor CPE), so counts are not comparable with self-hosted platforms
Few core CVEs per year (3 in 2025, 3 in 2026 to date) but 141 module advisories from Friends-of-Presta in 2023 and a critical ps_facetedsearch CVE in 2026 (CVSS 10); core ships no CSP support

Predictable monthly vendor bulletins and hotfixes, but 6 Adobe Commerce entries in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue (including CVE-2022-24086, CosmicSting, SessionReaper and CVE-2026-75650) and long-running Magecart skimming of unpatched stores

Few core CVEs (16 in total) but 11,334 new WordPress ecosystem vulnerabilities in 2025, 91% in plugins (Patchstack), keyword CVE count 893 in 2026 to date, and the 2021 forced update and CVE-2023-28121 incidents
EUR 32 to 384 per month (billed monthly) plus 1.3 to 2.1% + EUR 0.30 card fees and 0.2 to 2% on third-party gateways; Plus from EUR 2,100 per month; hosting included
Free software; the merchant pays hosting, paid modules and development (no reliable figure, so the score reflects the zero licence and moderate infrastructure needs)
Open Source is free but needs heavy hosting and specialist development; Adobe Commerce licence is quote-based (no public price)
Free plugin; hosting, theme and paid extensions extra; WooPayments 2.9% + USD 0.30 per US card with no monthly fee
Liquid themes, theme blocks, apps and Functions allow wide changes, but server code, the checkout and the data model are constrained (full checkout control only on Plus)
Open PHP/Symfony code, hooks, overrides, services and a new Hummingbird theme; every layer can be modified
Dependency injection, plugins, preferences, observers, layout XML and declarative schema make nearly every behaviour replaceable at the cost of complexity
Open code with actions, filters, CRUD classes, block extensibility and the whole WordPress theme and plugin ecosystem
Managed infrastructure scales with traffic (peak events) and Plus supports high-volume stores; limits are API rate limits and plan caps
Scales by sizing hosting and caching yourself; the platform targets small and mid-size catalogues and its median Lighthouse score is the lowest of the four on mobile (0.345)
Designed for large catalogues and traffic with indexers, message queues and cloud/PaaS editions; needs significant infrastructure and tuning
Scales with WordPress hosting and caching; high-order-volume stores need HPOS (custom order tables) and careful plugin selection
Storefront API, Customer Account API, Hydrogen (React framework) and Oxygen hosting; headless is a first-class, documented path
Webservice and the new Admin API expose data, but there is no official headless storefront framework or storefront API
GraphQL and REST APIs, PWA Studio and the headless Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service storefront; requires heavy integration work
REST API v3 and the Store API support headless use; no official storefront framework; GraphQL requires a community plugin
